title: A join-rules lock left by a killed writer is never recovered automatically: every later write for that tenant, including an opt-out, fails with `locked` until a human deletes the .lock file
area: packages/meeting-bot/src/calendar/join-rules-store-lock.ts acquireLock (stale branch throws, never takes over)
evidence: Checker probe on 6be3337: child process holding the lock inside recordTenantOptOut (afterRead sleeping), taskkill /F; `<tenant>.lock` remains; recordTenantOptOut(dir,"ta","e2",{lockWaitMs:1000}) -> JoinRulesStoreError locked after 1021 ms; with lockStaleMs:200 -> locked with the stale message (path, age 3s, content {token,pid,at}, "NOT stealing it ... delete the file ... by hand"); message accurate, manual delete restores service (recordTenantOptOut OK). Fails loudly and writes nothing, so no entry is lost; but an unattended service that cannot record an opt-out will join a meeting the user refused.
fix_direction: Not a merge blocker; a PRECONDITION for wiring the store into the unattended host. Either (a) the host surfaces locked/stale errors to the operator with the runbook and an alert, or (b) acquireLock takes over a lock whose recorded pid is not alive on this machine and whose age exceeds staleMs, re-reading the token after takeover (residual risk: pid reuse).
reproduction: cd packages/meeting-bot; node --import tsx stale.mjs (scratch probe): spawn child that calls recordTenantOptOut with afterRead=Atomics.wait 60s; taskkill /F /PID child; call recordTenantOptOut(dir,tenant,id,{lockWaitMs:1000}) -> locked.
